Aurelia Skyways Companion Animal Travel Desk incident report: This matter was reported by the senior coordinator after a routine review of desk activity and customer handling. The report concerns a service disruption during ordinary travel support for a live animal booking, where the record and the traveler guidance did not align at first contact. The issue was brought forward in a calm manner and was handled under the standard stepwise review used for escalations.

The matter began when a traveler contacted the Companion Animal Travel Desk to confirm acceptance details for a pet movement already under discussion. During the exchange, staff noted that the supporting information was incomplete and that the traveler had received an earlier explanation that did not fully match the current service review. The desk agent paused the interaction, avoided making any unsupported commitment, and asked the senior coordinator to oversee the case. The animal remained with the traveler and no immediate safety concern was identified. The concern was administrative rather than operational, but it required prompt attention because the guidance given at the desk must remain clear and consistent.

The senior coordinator checked the booking notes, compared them with the current carriage rules, and confirmed that a correction was needed before the matter could proceed. The traveler was told that the desk would review the file carefully and provide a clear answer after verification. The coordinator then contacted the relevant service channel, corrected the wording in the record, and advised the team on the proper response for similar cases. Staff were reminded to use calm, plain language, to verify all supporting details before confirming acceptance, and to escalate early when any part of a pet travel case appears inconsistent.

Follow-up action was completed by updating the internal notes and reinforcing the stepwise review process for all future companion animal bookings. The desk also logged the event for trend review so that repeated confusion can be identified and reduced. No further disruption was observed after the correction, and the traveler received the revised guidance in an orderly manner. The incident closed with no harm to the animal and with improved handling controls for future desk work.
